purpose: Model how a material property event may change one or more property interests while preserving separate event, document, registration and legal-effect states.
core_principle: BEFORE STATE → EVENT → LEGAL RULE → CONDITIONS → REGISTRATION/OTHER EFFECT → AFTER STATE
rules: An event may affect multiple interest dimensions and must not be reduced to ownership alone.
Event date, document date and registration date remain separate.
A document evidencing an event does not automatically prove the resulting registered state.
Registration may be a condition of legal effect where the governing regime requires it.
Succession, conveyancing and registration remain distinct layers.
A mortgage or charge event changes security state, not automatically ownership state.
A court order changes the legal analysis only within the order's actual scope and applicable registration framework.
An easement or boundary event must not be treated as an ownership transfer unless the governing law establishes that effect.
Historical state reconstruction requires evidence matching the target date.
hard_stops: Never infer the after-state from the event name alone.
Never treat inheritance as automatic registered transfer.
Never treat sale as automatic mortgage discharge.
Never treat a court order as self-executing registration without checking the applicable framework.
Never collapse multiple affected interest dimensions into one ownership label.
